_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: the mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so its (non-)oracle registration and catalog live here rather than in the shared ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🔣️oracle.json manifest. Line splitting, line-ending policy and trailing-newline handling are exactly what this subset ITSELF defines — no third-party crate is authoritative over 'is this a text file's line structure' the way lopdf is authoritative over PDF or png is authoritative over PNG, so no oracle is registered here (see noOracleDecisions below).

oracles.rationale: 📖️ A READER, registered separately from this file's existing `cross-semio-implementation` entry, which COMPUTES what a mutation should produce from this repository's own reading of the spec and therefore cannot discharge this requirement — both halves would descend from one reading of it. bstr 1.13.1 (BurntSushi's byte-string library) is a from-scratch UTF-8-aware byte-string crate, independent of this repository's own text handling. `bytes.is_utf8()` independently validates well-formed UTF-8, `bytes.lines()` splits on the real line-ending bytes present (witnessing `insert-line`/`remove-line`/`set-line`/`set-line-ending`), and `bytes.ends_with(b"\n")` witnesses `set-trailing-newline`. Verified against this subset's own committed `shared://🔤️.txt`: `is_utf8()` reported true, `lines().count()` the real 158 lines, and `ends_with(b"\n")` the real trailing newline.

noOracleDecisions.rationale:
There is no credible third-party crate that is authoritative over plain-text line structure: line splitting on LF/CRLF, uniform-per-document line-ending policy and trailing-newline presence are exactly what THIS subset defines. The closest candidate, the `csv` crate already linked for the tabular subsets, genuinely helps for a NARROW part of this: with quoting disabled and a delimiter byte that cannot appear in real text, its record reader independently confirms this subset's own line-boundary splitting on single-style, NON-BLANK real content — but a standalone probe found `csv-core`'s NFA silently treats a zero-byte record as "not a record" and never emits it (confirmed unconditionally, not a `Terminator`-mode artifact), so it cannot cross-check the true line count on any real prose that has blank lines at all, which most real text does (the real fixture has 80, measured). It cannot discharge a full differential comparison either way: it collapses LF/CR/CRLF into one undifferentiated boundary and never reports which terminator it saw, so it cannot confirm or refute this subset's central claim. THAT SURVEY STANDS AND IS UNCHANGED.

WHAT DOES NOT STAND is what this decision named as standing in an oracle's place: "an independently hand-written reference implementation of the mutation semantics in this subset's own oracle module, which never calls this subset's production `TxtSnapshot`/`TxtMutation` code". That description is accurate and the module is real — `oracle_apply_mutation`, `oracle_inverse_spec`, `independent_split`, `independent_render`, `project_txt` in `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🧪️oracle` — but it is OUR code, in OUR language, in OUR crate, by OUR authors, and under the raised bar it is not a second PRODUCER. Two implementations that share a language, a toolchain, a review culture and an author agree about the things that culture agrees about; the whole value of a second producer is that it does not. This decision is therefore a DEBT, not a judgement, and is recorded as one.

WHAT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION HERE WOULD BE WRITTEN FROM, and why this case is one of the cheapest conversions left in the repository: `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` states the whole document — `{schema, lines[], trailingNewline, lineEnding ∈ {lf, crLf}}` — the seven verbs are `no-mutation`, `set-snapshot`, `set-trailing-newline`, `set-line-ending`, `insert-line`, `remove-line` and `set-line`, and the NINE literal `@id-spec-vector` byte vectors carried inline in this feature (pure LF, pure CRLF, no trailing terminator, mixed CRLF and bare LF, a BOM as first-line content, astral emoji and variation selectors, combining marks, and NEL/LS/PS explicitly NOT treated as separators) pin the split-and-render contract byte for byte, in any language. It also reads a REAL 27,471-byte artifact — a 170-line German interview transcript with genuine umlauts and 80 real blank lines — which is more than most converted cases in this wave can say.

WHAT BLOCKS IT TODAY, precisely, and it is not the specification. First, the ORACLE ROLE OF THIS CASE IS ALREADY OCCUPIED, and occupied differently from every other case in this group. Thirteen of the eighteen remaining Group-A cases do register Rust `.oracle(...)` handlers — measured, not assumed — but those handlers read the committed vector through `include_str!` and hand it back, and a recorded no-oracle case dispatches no oracle role at all, so they are DEAD CODE that reads as coverage in a listing and would not be a second producer if they ran. This case is the one where the reference half is a genuinely separate hand-written implementation, and it lives in ANOTHER OWNER'S CRATE: `semio_s_plugin_stdio_test_oracle::artifacts::txt::…::{oracle_apply_mutation, oracle_inverse_spec, independent_split, independent_render, project_txt}`. Converting therefore means MOVING the reference role out of that module rather than adding one beside it, and the module would lose its only consumer for this subset. That is a deliberate change to another owner's file and is not made unilaterally here. Second, the projection this case compares is a `TxtSnapshot` whose `schema` member is the Rust constant `crate::artifacts::txt::STDIO_TXT_DOCUMENT_SCHEMA`; its VALUE is stated in no committed document, so a second implementation cannot emit the projection without being told the constant — the same class of gap `mutate-program-1` reports for its child-addressing function, at a much smaller scale. Publishing that schema string in `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` as a `const` and moving the oracle registration are the two edits that unblock this case.

WHAT IS ASSERTED IN THE MEANTIME is unchanged: the nine literal byte-exact specification vectors, the inverse law as a metamorphic property over the real transcript, and the carrier law that the re-encoded bytes are bit-identical to the input. The ceiling is that both sides of every comparison are Rust written in this repository.

[C2 2026-09-02] Narrowed `capabilities` to remove 'txt-utf-8-mutate': a mutation manifest already requires an external-oracle discharge for this capability (tracked honestly as `missing-external-oracle`), so a no-oracle decision claiming the same capability made that gap invisible to `no-oracle-covers-mutation` without discharging it. The rationale above is kept verbatim as the record of what was actually investigated; only the claim is withdrawn. See .🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️02/SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION/📓️c2-native-artifact-oracles.md.
